A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have studied how dental tissue matrices, such as dentine and cementum, can induce the proliferation and differentiation of human dental pulp stem cells (DPSC).

we have shown that DPSC are able to differentiate into odontogenic lineages, such as cementoblasts and odontoblasts, in a tridimensional matrix of non-mineralised dentin and cementum, and that this differentiation was influenced by the composition and the tridimensional structure of the matrix.

the dental pulp is a tissue with a high regenerative potential, since it is composed of a heterogeneous population of cells that includes a subpopulation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) with a great potential of self-renewal, proliferation and multi-lineage differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dentin matrix is a good substrate for human DPSCs.
dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) can be induced to differentiate towards odontoblastic lineage in vitro.
